newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 19.

text.p: A Wellington nurse survived the massacre in Chechnya that claimed six of her Red Cross co-workers, including fellow Wellingtonian Sheryl Thayer. Louisa Akavi was in the Red Cross compound when masked killers struck before dawn on Tuesday. The gunmen appear to have deliberately targeted overseas workers, going from room to room using guns with silencers to slaughter the workers in the bloodiest attack against the Red Cross in its 133-year history. Page 1.

ACT NZ would refuse to support the government till it revealed the content of secret coalition deals, ACT leader Richard Prebble said on Wednedsay. He said supporting the government while some matters remained unpublished would amount to signing a blank piece of paper. Prebble has written to Prime Minister Jim Bolger asking urgently that he publish all agreements reached with NZ First. Page 2.

New Zealand will formally request Japan not to ship plutonium waste through New Zealand waters, after news of plans for a shipment of the radioactive substance to travel south next month. News of the shipment, due to leave France on January 16 for Japan via South Africa, Australia and the South Pacific was made public by Greenpeace on Wednesday. Page 2.

New Zealand and the European Union on Wednesday signed a ground-breaking veterinary agreement covering animal and animal product trade, which could save the New Zealand meat industry millions of dollars a year. Page 2.

Business confidence slumped in December across all sectors, except construction, according to the National Bank's latest Business Outlook survey. The survey was carried out early in the month before the coalition government was confirmed, but there were signs that the tax cuts would be delayed and government spending lifted. A net seven percent of those surveyed expect business conditions to improve in the next 12 months, compared with a net 20 percent in November. The delayed tax cuts appeared to be a "body blow" to confidence in the service and retail sectors and the labour markets. Page 17.

The Commerce Commission has cleared Telecom of cross-subsidising its Xtra Internet service, but will continue to investigate Xtra's losses as a possible breach of the Commerce Act. The commission will look into whether Xtra is being used by Telecom as a loss-leader to eliminate Internet competition, a practice prohibited by section 36 of the Act. "There is evidence that Xtra's pricing may have a detrimental effect on competition and this may indicate the purpose of the pricing strategy," said commision chairman Alan Bollard. Page 17.

Former finance minister Ruth Richardson said new language requiring the Reserve Bank to consider sustainable growth, employment and development opportunities was a flimflam pulled on Treasurer Winston Peters and did not change the bank's focus on inflation. Reserve Bank governor Don Brash signed the previous policy targets agreement with Richardson, defining price stability as zero to two percent. "It is clear the policy targets agreement has been preserved in all its essentials," Richardson said on Wednesday. "The words chosen are cosmetic...perhaps Winston doesn't understand that." Page 17.

ANZ and PostBank dropped their mortgage lending rates on Wednesday to the lowest levels for almost two years, joining other big banks that moved on Tuesday. The two dropped their variable mortgage rates to 9.95 percent from 10.65 percent for new loans from December 23 and for existing customers from February 3. The one-year fixed rate will fall to 9.5 percent from 9.95 percent, also effective from December 23 and the three-year fixed rate will stay at 8.95 percent. The base rate for small business falls to 10.95 percent from 11.75 percent. Page 17.

Two New Zealand boat builders are key figures in Japanese car giant Toyota's plunge into the Japanese marine market. Reuters reported Toyota's plan to enter the marine industry from Tokyo on Wednesday, naming McDell Marine and Circa Engineering and Marine as the builders of 15 28-foot cabin cruisers to be marketed in Japan next year. Toyota designed and developed the cruisers, though they will be built in New Zealand. Page 17.

The planned referendum on compulsory superannuation could put the brakes on gains made in voluntary savings in recent years, retirement savings groups say. A referendum is expected in 1998 as part of the coalition deal between National and NZ First. Superannuation companies want the government to give a clear indication that any savings scheme will not penalise those with existing retirement savings plans. Page 19.
